newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up at 20-month high against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up at 20-month high against dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed in Shanghai on Tuesday at a 20-month high of 8.2940 against the U.S. dollar, up from Monday's 8.2947.
It was the currency's highest close since May 19, 1995, when it ended at 8.2925.
The yuan opened down at an intraday low of 8.2952 and moved gradually up from 8.2947 to 8.2942 before hitting an intraday high of 8.2932 late in trading.
Trading was active with most done at about 8.2942, traders said.
Dealers said higher demand for the yuan before the Chinese lunar new year holiday and reduced central bank intervention had pushed the currency upwards in the past few weeks.
One dealer said pro-yuan sentiment was pushing the yuan higher.
"But fear of central bank intervention at high price levels is keeping buyers from pushing the yuan up sharply," he said.

State media on Tuesday quoted Zhou Xiaoquan, head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, as saying the yuan would remain stable and the foreign exchange market would improve throughout 1997.
His remarks had no direct impact on yuan movements on Tuesday, one dealer said.
"It is macro-economic policy, which does not affect day-to-day movement," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to consolidate around 8.2940 on Wednesday.
The yuan closed up at 6.9160 from 6.9500 against 100 Japanese yen and up slightly at 1.0713 from 1.0715 against the Hong Kong dollar.
